title: The shipped pre-commit gate reports its scope only on failure, so a gate enforcing nothing is silent and looks identical to one enforcing everything
body:
The shipped pre-commit gate reports its enforcement scope ONLY when something went wrong, so a gate that ran ZERO critics is silent and is indistinguishable from a gate that enforced everything. This ships to every consumer project on its next upgrade, which is what separates it from the estate-internal reach gap it was found beside.

THE MECHANISM, read at `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh`:

  458  LANGS=()
  459  if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "intent/.config/config.json" ]; then
  ...      LANGS+=("$lang")   # from (.languages // [])
  505  UNENFORCED=()
  511  if [ "${#LANGS[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then   # the whole dispatch loop
  592  if [ "${#UNENFORCED[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  594    echo "intent critic gate: ${#UNENFORCED[@]} of ${#LANGS[@]} declared language(s) went UNENFORCED"

THREE ROUTES REACH `LANGS=()`, and all three are silent: `jq` is not installed; `intent/.config/config.json` is absent; the `languages` array is empty. Each leaves the dispatch loop unentered, `UNENFORCED` empty, and the report at 592 suppressed. The gate then exits having run no critic and having said nothing about it.

THE FILE'S OWN COMMENT, four lines above the emission, STATES THE PROPERTY THE CODE DOES NOT PROVIDE:

  # **THE DENOMINATOR IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART.** `1 of 5` is a bad day; `5 of 5`
  # is a gate that is not running at all, and those must never look alike.

That reasoning is correct and it is applied one level too low. It distinguishes `1 of 5` from `5 of 5` and does not distinguish either from `0 of 0`, which is the case it was written for.

`jq` DESERVES ITS OWN LINE. `command -v jq` failing disarms every language critic in the gate with no message on any path. A consumer project on a machine without `jq` has a pre-commit gate that runs, prints its other guards, exits 0, and enforces no rules.

COVERAGE, WHICH IS WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. The estate's instrument for denominator honesty is `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/of_n_labels_its_derivation.sh`. Its default population is `$HERE/*.sh` -- its own directory -- while its docstring claims every instrument emitting an `N of M` at all. `lib/templates/hooks/` is outside that reach, so no instrument has ever examined this ratio. The operands themselves ARE derived (both arrays are built by `+=` in loops), so this is a coverage gap rather than a laundered figure; the point is that nothing established that.

A SECOND OBSERVATION, NOT A CLAIM. The identical block appears at `lib/templates/hooks/critic-guard.sh:371-381`, byte-for-byte including the comment, and nothing in the tree dispatches that file by name. MODULES.md records it as the critic gate as a guard BODY, deliberately unrostered, with carriers running it. It is mine and the arrangement may be transitional, so whether this is a Highlander violation or an intended two-carrier shape is NOT established here.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the gate states its scope on every path it can take, including the path where the scope is zero, and says which of the three routes produced a zero.


---

**FIXED 2026-09-05 at `47a17528`, `ratified_in: "vc, 2026-09-05, under hv's pen granted 2026-08-22"`** (vc withdrew an escalation of `0266` on hv's standing directive that there is no external consumer and everything outstanding goes into 3.0.1, and this row came with it).

The scope line is now UNCONDITIONAL, and the zero NAMES ITS ROUTE.

## The two rules in this file were in tension and the resolution is the useful part

This file already says **a report that never changes trains its reader to stop looking**, and it also says **`1 of 5` is a bad day, `5 of 5` is a gate that is not running, and those must never look alike.** An always-printed scope line appears to violate the first.

**It does not, because the line CHANGES rather than appears.** `1 of 1 declared language(s) enforced (shell)` and `0 of 0 -- NO code critic ran in this commit` are different text on the same line. The old behaviour was one line present and one line absent, and **an absence is not a report** -- there is nothing for a reader to fail to notice.

## Driven, with the controls on the INSTRUMENT and not only on the subject

The decisive pair is one project with `languages: ["shell"]` declared, committed twice, the only difference being `jq`:

```
  jq absent   ->  intent critic gate: 0 of 0 declared language(s) -- NO code critic ran in this commit.
                    why: jq is not installed, so the declared languages could not be read at all --
                    every language critic is disarmed on this machine, in every project
  jq present  ->  intent critic gate: 1 of 1 declared language(s) enforced (shell).
```

**Before the fix those two commits said the same thing: nothing.**

Controls: `jq` genuinely unreachable on the scrubbed PATH, and reachable on the normal one, so the scrub is what changed the answer. **The first attempt at that arm left `/usr/bin` on PATH, where `jq` also lives** -- it tested nothing and reported the `languages: []` reason instead. The arm looked like it had run. That control is the only reason it did not land here as evidence.

## A CORRECTION TO THIS ROW: it names three silent routes and only TWO can arrive

The absent-`config.json` case never reaches the language block. The project test near the top of the file `exit 0`s on it with its own message -- `not inside an Intent project (intent/.config/config.json absent); skipping` -- long before `LANGS` is built. That is the right home for it, because it is about being in an Intent project at all rather than about enforcement scope.

**The first build of this fix carried a branch for it anyway**: unreachable code reading as coverage, which is this row's own defect one level down. It was found by driving the route rather than by reading, and removed rather than kept as defence.

## Why it could be fixed at all, which was not obvious from the row

This row says the defect "ships to every consumer project on its next upgrade". On the **published** v3.0.0 that understates it in the other direction: the gate body is never invoked at all there, because `claude upgrade --apply` writes a chain block naming `.git/hooks/pre-commit.intent` and that build never writes the file (`0266`). **So on v3.0.0 this defect sits behind one that makes it unreachable.** At `HEAD` the carrier installer exists and the gate runs, which is where this fix takes effect.
